title: Friendship Without the Heart
note: He defines this as the friendship of enemies who never join you at heart, but stay close outwardly until they get their chance.

couplets.plain: The friendship of those who keep company without agreeing at heart is an anvil. When they find their chance, you are struck on it.
couplets.pm: The friendship of those who stay close without being at one with you, until they get their chance, then becomes an anvil. It seems to bear you up until the moment for the blow comes, and then lets you be cut right through. Some read a different word, and take the place to be the end.

links.reason: Turns the friendship of those not with you at heart into an anvil on which you will be struck.

links.quote: those who keep company without agreeing at heart
links.reason: Looks at what friendship means in the hands of someone who is an enemy at heart.

couplets.plain: The friendship of those who seem your own but are not will change, like the minds of women.
couplets.pm: Friendship with those who seem your own but aren’t changes, when they get their chance, as women’s minds change. For a friendship to change means going back to the old enmity.

links.quote: those who seem your own but are not
links.reason: Seems your own, is not, and will change when the chance comes.

couplets.plain: Even after learning many good things, it is hard for enemies to become good at heart.
couplets.pm: Even after learning many good books, which destroy faults of the mind, enemies don’t amend their minds and become friends. Becoming good means giving up hatred. Don’t take those with hatred within as friends because they are learned.

links.quote: hard for enemies to become good at heart
links.reason: Hate in an enemy’s heart outlasts even much good learning.

links.quote: Even after learning many good things

couplets.plain: Fear the deceivers who smile sweetly with the face and are bitter within.
couplets.pm: Fear the deceivers who smile sweetly at your face when they see you and are always bitter in the heart. They put on a smile that is the opposite of the hatred within. That hatred doesn’t show even on the face, the means of reading a person, so they are to be feared.

links.quote: smile sweetly with the face and are bitter within
links.reason: Warns to fear the smile that covers bitterness within.

couplets.plain: Those who don’t join you in their minds are not to be trusted in anything, on their words alone.
couplets.pm: The books of right conduct hold that those who don’t agree with you at heart aren’t to be trusted in any matter on the strength of their words. Don’t take deceitful words, spoken to hide enmity, as straight words and trust them with your affairs.

links.quote: not to be trusted in anything, on their words alone
links.reason: Words from those whose minds are not with you deserve no trust at all.

couplets.plain: They may say good things, as friends do, but the words of those who aren’t with you are soon seen for what they are.
couplets.pm: Enemies may speak words that seem to bring good, as friends do, but as they speak it is known that those words will bring none. “May” implies that they don’t usually speak so. They are enemies, so harm is certain, and it is known at once.

links.quote: soon seen for what they are
links.reason: Good words, spoken as friends speak, can’t hide the hostile speaker for long.

links.quote: the words of those who aren’t with you

couplets.plain: Don’t trust the bowing words of enemies. The bowing of a bow means harm.
couplets.pm: The bending of a bow means harm to whoever stands against it, so don’t think the bending of an enemy’s speech means you good. An archer’s purpose lies in the bending of his bow, and an enemy’s in the bending of his words. Take it as bending that means harm, and guard yourself in fear.

links.reason: Bowing speech from an enemy is a threat and not a courtesy.

links.quote: The bowing of a bow means harm
Don’t trust the bowing words of enemies
links.reason: Concerns the enemy who comes with bowing speech.

couplets.plain: A weapon hides in the joined hands of enemies, and in their tears too.
couplets.pm: To those who can read an enemy’s intent, a weapon lies hidden in his joined hands, and in his tears too. Enemies reassure you with hands and eyes, then draw the weapon to kill. Look for it and it shows even as they reassure you. They may show meekness in worship or weeping, but watch their intent and guard yourself.

links.quote: A weapon hides in the joined hands of enemies

links.reason: An enemy’s weeping is one more disguise for a hidden weapon.
Watches an enemy’s hands and tears for what they hide.

couplets.plain: Those who make much of you and despise you: make them laugh, and within that friendship hold them so that it dies.
couplets.pm: Enemies make much of friendship outwardly and scorn you within. The law of rulers is to stay in that friendship too, please them outwardly, and hold to them so that it dies within. Being one thing inside and another outside is wrong, but the books of statecraft hold that against enemies it is right.
couplets.sensitive: urges secretly crushing those who mock you

links.quote: make much of you and despise you
links.reason: Describes those who make much of you outwardly and despise you all the same.

couplets.plain: When the time comes for an enemy to be a friend, be friends with the face, and put friendship out of the heart.
couplets.pm: When the time comes that your enemies behave as friends, be friends with them on your face, give it up in your heart, and then drop even that. The time is when you can’t yet openly cast them off as enemies. So keep them off as far as you can.

links.quote: be friends with the face, and put friendship out of the heart
links.reason: Counsels a false front towards an enemy who turns friend, until you can drop it.
